Theme

wrist noun

also wrists, wrist bone

modern

Traupman 59, 409

prīmōris manus, prīmōris manūs f.

the wrist

Traupman’s phrase, the front part of the arm, after classical prīmōris, foremost (dentēs prīmōrēs, the front teeth, Plin. NH 7.70; Lewis & Short). Classical Latin has no plain word for the wrist: the Romans spoke of the hand, manus, or of bracchium.

Other words

  • carpus, carpī m. — the wrist; the wrist bones

    noun, second declension · also used · modern · Traupman 59, 409 (wrist bone); Andresian p. 37

    The anatomists’ word, from Greek καρπός; not in Lewis & Short in this sense (there Carpus is a carver in Petronius).

Examples

  • manicae prōlixae ūsque in prīmōrēs manūs

    sleeves reaching all the way to the wristsTraupman 409

See also hand, arm, wristwatch, bracelet.

SourcesLewis & Short: primoris
